items.evidence: Would you mind checking these figures? - Not at all. Let me take a look.
Can someone cover my shift on Saturday? - I can, if it is the morning shift.
Who is responsible for arranging the shipment? - Ask Ms. Chen in logistics.
Why has the presentation been postponed? - The client requested more time to review the data.
Do we need to print more brochures? - There are still several boxes in storage.
Has the conference room been booked? - Let me check the reservation calendar.
How will you get to the trade fair? - A colleague offered me a ride.
Is the application form available online? - The website is being updated; I can give you a paper copy.
An adverb is required to modify the verb completed.
A noun is required as the direct object of requested following the determiner a clear.
An adjective is required in parallel with attractive after the linking verb is.
The subject is 'The number of online orders', which takes a singular verb.
The plural subject 'Several members' requires the plural verb 'travel'.
The singular subject 'Every employee' takes the singular present tense verb 'has'.
The time marker 'Last month' requires the simple past tense 'exceeded'.
The presence of 'since she graduated' indicates an action starting in the past and continuing into the present, requiring 'has worked'.
An ongoing past action interrupted by another requires the past continuous tense 'was checking'.
Specific times of the day use the preposition 'at'.
Specific days and dates use the preposition 'on'.
Continuing up to a specific time uses the preposition 'until'.
